chunks.title: [CLO Beginner's Tutorial] Basic Production Process_Dress
chunks.content: ## Basic Manufacturing Process of a Dress in CLO This section explains the initial setup and panel preparation for dress production in CLO, focusing on the picture library, virtual model insertion, and panel editing techniques including symmetry, sewing lines, and sheet linking. - Open the picture library in CLO's Connect by selecting "Cloth Training" and searching for "core tools." - Load the "Core Tools Basic Process to Make a Dress" and the cloth picture library. - Insert a virtual model and place the model's face. - Note the initial garment version shows only one side; symmetrical panel matching is required. - Understand three opening methods for panels: symmetry open editor, sewing line open, and panel open. - Symmetry open editor allows symmetrical panel opening with linked editing and sewing lines on both sides. - Panel open opens panels symmetrically without links. - For this dress, only the front panel is opened; inside and base spaces are excluded, and left-right sides are not linked. - Use the edit sewing line tool (accessed via Shift + functional tab) to slave editing panels, preparing front and middle lines. - Use adjustment sheet tools to fill remaining sheets; copy, paste, and mirror sheets with three methods: - **Symmetrical sheet with sewing line:** linked editor and sewing line. - **Symmetrical sheet and link sheet:** linked editor but sewing line not linked. - **Cron link sheet:** symmetrical and linked editor, sewing line not linked. - Different sheet types are distinguished by external frame colors. - In 2D window, right-click remaining sheets and select "Cron link sheet" to copy and mirror sheets. - Arrange the front panel near the model’s shadow; sleeves placed beside front panel; back pieces opposite sleeves. - This layout clarifies the panel structure and improves sewing speed and accuracy. ## 2D and 3D Panel Arrangement This section covers the arrangement of garment panels on the 2D workspace and the 3D virtual model to prepare for sewing. - Use the 3D window to arrange panels on the model. - Select all panels (Ctrl + A) and use the green axis on the positioning ball to move panels upward to avoid blocking views. - Use the arrangement points and positioning ball to fine-tune panel placement. - Switch views using the keyboard shortcut (8 key) to arrange back panels. - Use Shift to select multiple panels and move them using axis controls (green for vertical, blue for depth). - Gold-colored panels are reserved for later sewing. - Press Shift + F to check if panels are ready for sewing. ## Sewing Process and Tools This section details the sewing sequence, tool usage, and panel-specific sewing considerations for accurate garment construction. - Use 2D and 3D windows to select sewing tools and add sewing lines. - Sew panels from top to bottom to avoid missing seams. - Use Shift to sew pairs efficiently. - Sew front and back pieces first, then sew all parts together.
chunks.content_description: CLO Beginner Course introduces the basic process of virtual garment creation, using a basic dress as an example to master the fundamental operations of making a 3D garment in CLO.

chunks.content: - Press Shift + F to check if panels are ready for sewing. ## Sewing Process and Tools This section details the sewing sequence, tool usage, and panel-specific sewing considerations for accurate garment construction. - Use 2D and 3D windows to select sewing tools and add sewing lines. - Sew panels from top to bottom to avoid missing seams. - Use Shift to sew pairs efficiently. - Sew front and back pieces first, then sew all parts together. - Use free sewing tool to align front and back pieces according to cutout positions. - For multiple sewing pairs, press Shift to sew pairs. - Use switching position tool to adjust and complete sewing lines. - Sew sleeves last to tighten panel pieces. - Sleeve panel pieces initially have a blue-purple basic line used for marking. - Convert basic lines to internal lines using the loop outline tool in the 2D toolbar: - Select basic line, press Return to complete loop. - Use editing panel tool to confirm line turns red-brown (internal line). - Add sewing lines to sleeve panel pieces; overlapping sewing lines must be selected carefully. - Add loose panel pieces to the inside of sleeve panel pieces via right-click in 3D window and selecting "Add to Inside." - Complete all sewing lines before simulation. ## Simulation and Clothing Adjustment This section explains how to simulate the garment’s physical behavior, adjust panel layers for double-layer garments, and change model postures for better fitting and visualization. - Press Ctrl to start simulation; garment responds to sewing lines and gravity, ready to wear. - Use mouse/hand tool to adjust clothing fit during simulation. - For double-layer structures (e.g., front panel): - Use adjustment panel tool to select outer panel piece. - Right-click and choose the outer panel piece. - Switching to sewing line editor shows automatically generated sewing lines between layers. - A new panel piece layer is added to the 3D garment. - Simulate again to confirm double-layer effect. - Change model posture for fitting check: - Press Y to open posture drawing library. - Select and drag vertical female posture to 3D window. - Default model posture is double-layer, convenient for simulation. - Posture change helps assess wear and tear effects better. - Cancel posture drawing with Y again. ## Panel Line Display and Fabric Application This section addresses visualization of garment lines and fabric application to different panels for realistic appearance and behavior. - Blue lines on clothing and red lines on sleeves represent basic and inner panel lines. - Toggle line display off/on via clothing information display in 3D window menu bar to better visualize fabric. - Apply fabric: - Open drawing library (Y), select fabric category in Connect. - Search for "lace," select lace gauze fabric, and add to object window. - Confirm and close picture library. - Open Color tool and search for color number 114101; add it to custom color palette. - Select sleeves and outer front panels (Shift to multi-select).

chunks.content: - Toggle line display off/on via clothing information display in 3D window menu bar to better visualize fabric. - Apply fabric: - Open drawing library (Y), select fabric category in Connect. - Search for "lace," select lace gauze fabric, and add to object window. - Confirm and close picture library. - Open Color tool and search for color number 114101; add it to custom color palette. - Select sleeves and outer front panels (Shift to multi-select). - Apply lace fabric to selected panels. - Use Cloth Sketchbook to apply fabric effects like V2, shrink, and bulge by dragging onto fabric. - Rename fabric as needed. - For elastic band panels (e.g., sleeve elastic bands), select panels in 2D window (Shift select multiple). - Apply elastic band fabric from sketchbook. - Close sketchbook and simulate to observe fabric effects on wrinkles and wear. - Close simulation after review. ## Elastic Ratio and Fabric Stretch Optimization This section explains how to manage elastic ratios and adjust fabric stretch properties to prevent unwanted deformation. - Use edit panel tool to select neckline. - Observe 3D line length is longer than 2D line, indicating fabric stretch. - To prevent stretching: - Select sleeve panels (Shift multi-select). - In attribute editor, find Elastic section with elastic ratio and strength parameters. - Elastic ratio controls simulated shrinkage; default is 80%, meaning 3D line is 80% of original length. - Strength indicates resistance to stretch; higher strength means less stretch. - Set elastic ratio to 100% on neckline to avoid stretching. - For back waist and long edge seams, also set elastic ratio to 100% to maintain shape. - Select multiple lines and unify elastic ratio to 100%. - Adjust fabric angle as needed and simulate to observe changes. - Close simulation after confirming results. ## Improving Clothing Quality and Simulation Settings This section covers settings to enhance garment simulation quality, including particle diameter, thickness conflict, surface diameter, and simulation speed options. - Use the "Improve Quality" button in 3D toolbar. - Key parameters: - **Particle Diameter:** Distance between clothing grid points; smaller diameter means more detailed mesh but slower simulation. - **Thickness of Plate Conflict:** Safety distance on garment surface preventing protrusions during simulation; default 2.5 mm, can be reduced to 1 mm when particle diameter is smaller. - **Surface Diameter of Model:** Safety distance between garment and model surface; default 3 mm, reducing it makes clothing closer to model. - **Simulation Quality:** Choose between normal speed (faster, balanced accuracy) and test wear speed (slower, more physically accurate fabric simulation). - Recommended settings for detailed simulation: - Particle diameter: 5 mm - Thickness conflict: 1 mm - Surface diameter: 0 mm - Simulation quality: normal speed - Apply settings and confirm. - Press Ctrl to start simulation; observe more delicate and realistic garment behavior. - Close simulation and return to front view. ## Saving and Error Handling This section describes saving the project and troubleshooting simulation-related errors.
chunks.content_description: CLO Beginner Course introduces the basic process of virtual garment creation, using a basic dress as an example to master the fundamental operations of making a 3D garment in CLO.

observe more delicate and realistic garment behavior. - Close simulation and return to front view. ## Saving and Error Handling This section describes saving the project and troubleshooting simulation-related errors. - Save the dress project by selecting File > Save Project File. - In case of errors or simulation file issues (e.g., fogged display), right-click in the 3D window and select "Flight Surface" to fix. - Confirm to clear display anomalies. - Change layer color if needed to remove unwanted glaze or visual artifacts. - Adjust tolerance settings (e.g., to 10 degrees) to refine garment behavior and appearance.
